items.title: Ex-Cop Sentenced to Chemical Castration After He Was Convicted of Child Rape
items.summary:
A former Louisiana police officer and volunteer firefighter convicted of raping children was sentenced to three life prison sentences and castration as an additional punishment.

Kedreyon K. Williams , of New Roads, was found guilty in October of three counts of first-degree child rape, indecent behavior with a child and possession of pornography involving children following a four-day trial, according to the 18th Judicial District Attorney’s Office .

“A rape conviction automatically carries a mandatory sentence of life in prison, but District Attorney Tony Clayton went a step further and filed the motion for castration,” the office said in a Friday, November 13, news release.

In 2024, Louisiana became the first state to legalize surgical castration as punishment for people convicted of sex crimes against a child younger than 12, according to the Associated Press . Louisiana and a few other states also allow for chemical castration in cases involving sex crime convictions.

“He performed disgusting acts on children who could not defend themselves,” Clayton said in a statement. “He is a child predator and he deserves exactly what he is getting and more.”

“The castration is another layer of punishment for these horrendous crimes,” Clayton added. “If a man takes sexual advantage of a child, and we will take his manhood!”

Williams, who previously worked as a New Roads…

items.title: Man Hit Mother With Her Own Car After She Tracked It Down With Hidden AirTag

John Tiffin was charged with second-degree murder in connection to the death of his mother, Karen Curthoys . Tiffin, 31, was also charged with assault and battery with a dangerous weapon and reckless driving and obstructing an officer.

The Tulsa Police Department said in a Thursday, November 12, press release that the incident began in September when Tiffin borrowed his mother’s car. Conflict evolved when he refused to give it back to Curthoys, 69, after weeks of having the vehicle despite “the expectation that he’d give it back.”

Authorities said that Curthoys and one of her other children eventually managed to track the car down by using an AirTag that had been hidden in the collar of the victim’s dog, who was with Tiffin at the time of the incident, according to court documents obtained by KTUL .

“The victim stood in the driveway between the car she arrived in and the car Tiffin hadn’t returned,” police said in the press release. “Tiffin and his boyfriend were in the car, and the brother opened the car door to confront them. Authorities notified them of the identification of her remains.

It was also reported that he had a “droopy” and “flushed face,” “droopy” eyelids, “glassy eyes,” a “blank stare and dilated pupils.”
